zh.title: 馬來西亞暫停飛行醫生航班 直昇機墜毀五人罹難
zh.summary: 砂拉越飛醫停飛安檢；五人罹難，調查進行中；
body: 馬來西亞已暫停砂拉越的「飛行醫生服務」航班以進行安全檢視，此前一架直升機墜毀，造成一名飛行員和四名醫療人員罹難。衛生部長Dzulkefly Ahmad於2026年9月10日宣布暫停服務，事發於9月8日直升機在婆羅洲砂拉越Long Lellang跑道附近墜毀後兩天。
官員表示，緊急醫療後送將透過與消防與救援部門合作持續進行。衛生部也在討論可能的軍方援助，以運送需要緊急治療的病患。

該直升機的營運商Layang-Layang Aerospace，自願暫停其BO-105直升機及其他使用勞斯萊斯250引擎系列機隊的運作，依據民航局執行長Captain Norazman Mahmud所述。他強調，此暫係預防性措施，並未確立引擎或其他部件導致這起事故。CAAM正在監督營運商的檢查，並審查飛機、營運商與駕駛員紀錄。社群媒體上的影片顯示，直升機在墜毀起火前，曾以控制方式飛行，但拖曳濃厚灰色煙霧。
涉及事故的直升機為一架註冊編號9MFF的BO-105，於2026年9月8日執行醫療任務。警方描述其航程從美里出發，服務包括Long Lell朗在內的多個偏遠社區。
五名罹難者分別為駕駛員Zain Zal Afiq Afif Aisham、醫療醫官Azil A،ح азот،،،،،،،，
馬來西亞航空事故調查局（隸屬交通部）正進行調查。交通部副部長Hahzili Habib osman於2026年9月11日表示，調查人員已在現場。Norazman表示，初步報告預計在30天內出爐，完整報告則需一年。
這起事故也擾亂了定期載客服務。Airborne表示，Long Lellung跑道暫停商業營運，迫使該公司將兩班於9月9日往返美里與Long拉朗之間的航班調整至9月11日。

en.title: Malaysia suspends Flying Doctor flights after Sarawak helicopter crash kills five
en.summary: Sarawak Flying Doctor flights suspended for safety review after a helicopter crash killed a pilot and four medical workers.
body: Malaysia has suspended Flying Doctor Service flights in Sarawak for a safety review after a helicopter crash killed a pilot and four medical workers. Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad announced the service suspension on September 10, 2026, two days after the helicopter crashed near Long Lellang airstrip in the Malaysian state on Borneo.

Emergency medical evacuations will continue through cooperation with the Fire and Rescue Department, officials said. The ministry is also discussing possible military assistance to transport patients needing urgent treatment.

The helicopter's operator, Layang-Layang Aerospace, voluntarily halted operations of its BO-105 helicopters and other aircraft in its fleet using Rolls-Royce 250-series engines, according to Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia CEO Captain Norazman Mahmud. He stressed that the grounding was precautionary and did not establish that an engine or another component caused the accident. CAAM is monitoring the operator's inspections and reviewing aircraft, operator and pilot records. Video posted to social media showed the helicopter flying under control but trailing thick gray smoke before it crashed and burst into flames.

The helicopter involved, a BO-105 registered 9M-LLF, was conducting a medical mission on September 8, 2026. Police described an itinerary from Miri serving several remote communities, including Long Lellang.
The five people killed were pilot Captain Hazemat, Hazem Your Afinn, and four medical workers, and the victims were photographed elsewhere.

Malaysia's Air Accident Investigation Bureau, part of the Transport Ministry, is investigating. Deputy Transport Minister Hasbi Habibollah said on September 11, 2026, that investigators were at the site. Nor Azim said an initial report was expected within 30 days and a final report within a year.

The crash also disrupted scheduled passenger services. AirBorneo said Long Lellang airstrip temporarily closed to commercial operations, prompting it to move two September 9 flights between Miri and Long Lellang to September 11.

zh.title: Frontier Airlines宣布12月開航哥倫比亞三航線
zh.summary: Frontier Airlines 12月首開南美哥倫比亞三航線；仍待政府核准
body: Frontier Airlines 宣布將於2026年12月開闢其首批南美洲航線，以佛羅里達州奧蘭多為樞紐，連接哥倫比亞的波哥大、美德因及卡塔赫納。
這家美國廉價航空公司在2026年9月10日公布此擴張計畫。三條航線均仍須經由政府核准。
美德因航線每日一班於12月10日開辦，波哥大航線於12月14日開辦，推出初期每週六班，並於2027年3月6日起增至每日一班；卡塔赫納每週一班服務則於12月19日開始。
Frontier Airlines 表示，初期單程票價由波哥大的99美元、美德因的169美元及卡塔赫納的129美元起，適用於2027年1月14日至4月5日間的部分日期。該公司規劃以空中巴士A320系列機型營運這些航線。

en.title: Frontier Airlines plans first South America flights with three Colombia routes
en.summary: Frontier Airlines plans December 2026 launch of Orlando-Colombia routes to Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena
body: Frontier Airlines has announced plans to launch its first South American flights in December 2026, connecting Orlando with Bogotá, Medellín and Cartagena in Colombia.
The US low-cost carrier announced the expansion on September 10, 2026. All three routes remain subject to government approval.

Daily Medellín flights begin December 10, followed by Bogotá on December 14. Bogotá will initially operate six times weekly, increasing to daily on March 6, 2027. Weekly Cartagena service starts December 19.

Introductory one-way fares start at $99 for Bogotá, $169 for Medellín and $129 for Cartagena, covering selected dates from January 14 through April 5, 2027. Frontier plans to operate the routes with Airbus A320-family aircraft.

zh.title: 杜拜規劃阿勒馬克圖機場地下油罐因應襲擊
zh.summary: 杜拜航空考慮阿勒馬克圖機場地下油罐；DXB遭襲後規劃防護
body: 杜拜航空（Dubai Airports）正考慮在阿勒馬克圖國際機場（DWC）將航空燃油儲罐移至地下，並加固其他關鍵基礎設施，以因應2026年伊朗衝突期間杜拜國際機場（DXB）地上設施遭襲擊的教訓。
杜拜計劃將業務從DXB遷移至擴建後的DWC，此舉為下一代航空樞紐設計提供了納入衝突經驗的機會。杜拜航空執行長Paul Griffiths表示，規劃人員正審視包括航空燃油儲存在內的脆弱設施，是否應置於地下或加強防護，以抵禦未來無人機與飛彈攻擊。
衝突於2月28日爆發，導致區域空域嚴重受阻，DXB上半年旅客吞吐量銳減31.3%，僅達3,150萬人次，較2025年同期約4,600萬人次大幅下降；起降架次亦減少32.1%。DXB地上油罐遭擊中，迫使機場一度暫停運營，但Griffiths稱機場迅速恢復飛行。
Griffiths在《金融時報》訪談中透露，衝突期間共發出111次警報，其中17次導致實際襲擊，多數僅造成表面損傷。他強調，與阿聯酋當局及軍方的緊密協調，讓機場能快速應對威脅、疏散旅客至安全區域。
為提升韌性，DWC設計正評估將油罐地下化及其他設施「硬化」。Griffiths指出：「某些基礎設施可能需要加固，以應對未來可能的活動，使其更具韌性。」他補充說，地下儲油是設計過程中考慮的選項之一，「關鍵在於襲擊可能性與後果之間的平衡，以及適當的風險評估。」

en.title: Dubai Plans Underground Fuel Tanks at Al Maktoum After DXB Strikes
en.summary: Dubai Airports considers underground fuel tanks at Al Maktoum after DXB strikes
body: Dubai Airports is considering placing aviation fuel tanks underground and hardening other critical infrastructure at Al Maktoum International Airport (DWC) after above‑ground facilities at Dubai International Airport (DXB) were struck during the 2026 conflict involving Iran.

Dubai plans to transfer operations from DXB to an expanded DWC, creating an opportunity to incorporate lessons from the conflict into the design of its next‑generation aviation hub. Dubai Airports CEO Paul Griffiths said planners were examining whether vulnerable infrastructure, including aviation fuel storage, should be placed underground or reinforced against future drone and missile attacks.

The conflict, which began on 28 February 2026, severely disrupted regional airspace. In the first half of 2026 DXB handled 31.5 million passengers, down 31.3% from roughly 46 million in the same period of 2025, while aircraft movements fell 32.1%. Above‑ground fuel tanks were struck, forcing DXB to halt operations temporarily, though Griffiths said the airport resumed flights rapidly.

In an interview with the Financial Times, Griffiths disclosed that there were 111 alerts during the conflict, of which 17 resulted in strikes, with most causing only superficial damage. He said close coordination with UAE authorities and the military allowed airport staff to respond quickly to threats and move passengers to safer areas when necessary.

The experience is now shaping DWC’s design. Griffiths confirmed that important facilities, including fuel tanks, could be located underground, and other infrastructure may require additional reinforcement. He described the approach as a balance between the likelihood of an attack and its potential consequences: “Certain bits of the infrastructure may need to be a bit hardened against possible future activity, to make them more resilient.” Underground fuel storage is among the ideas under consideration, with Griffiths adding: “It’s about likelihood [of an attack] versus consequence and the proper risk.”
